title: Accurate sampling of undisturbed top sediment from grab sampler collected using aluminum tube and stainless-steel containers for shallow and deep-sea applications
author: Iizuka, Amano, et al.

steps.title: Wear protective clothing
steps.instruction: Put on natural rubber gloves and cotton workwear before any sampling operation.

steps.title: Prepare container and ventilation tube
steps.instruction: Select a stainless‑steel container (85 × 105 × 85 mm, 0.45 L) and clean it by ultrasonic treatment for 15 min, then rinse thoroughly with Milli‑Q water. Bend a J‑shaped aluminum tube (diameter 0.4 mm) 180° so that one arm is 350 mm long and the other is 200 mm long.

substeps.instruction: Ultrasonically treat the stainless‑steel container for 15 minutes.
Rinse the container with Milli‑Q water.
Bend the aluminum tube 180°; set lengths to 350 mm (long arm) and 200 mm (short arm).

steps.title: Insert container, collect sediment, seal
steps.instruction: After retrieving the K‑grab, position the stainless‑steel container with its opening downward, insert the short arm of the aluminum tube inside the container and leave the long arm outside, open the K‑grab lid, and carefully lower the container‑tube assembly into the sediment without blocking the tube. Remove surrounding sediment with a stainless‑steel scoop, slide a gloved hand beneath the container and lift it out, invert the container, level the sediment surface with a stainless‑steel spatula, wipe the rim with a cotton cloth, and finally seal the lid.

substeps.instruction: Place the container opening downward.
Insert the 200 mm tube arm into the container; keep the 350 mm arm external.
Open the K‑grab lid.
Lower the container‑tube assembly into the sediment, avoiding tube obstruction.
Use a stainless‑steel scoop to clear sediment around the container.
Insert a gloved hand beneath the container and extract it smoothly.
Invert the container.
Level the sediment surface with a stainless‑steel spatula.
Wipe container edges with a cotton cloth.
Seal the container lid.

steps.title: Transport sealed sample to laboratory
steps.instruction: Keep the sealed 0.45 L stainless‑steel container (or larger containers if used) in a protected position and ship it to the laboratory for further analysis following the referenced protocols.

steps.title: Prepare field blank for contamination check
steps.instruction: Fill a stainless‑steel container with Milli‑Q water, place it on the upper part of the K‑grab as a field blank, expose it during the sampling run, then retrieve it for laboratory processing.

substeps.instruction: Fill a stainless‑steel container with Milli‑Q water.
Position the container on the upper part of the K‑grab.
Expose the blank during the sediment‑sampling operation.
Recover the blank after the grab is retrieved.

steps.title: Process field blank in laboratory
steps.instruction: Rinse the field‑blank container, vacuum‑filter the rinse water, and evaluate any accumulated microplastics.

substeps.instruction: Rinse the field‑blank container.
Vacuum‑filter the rinse water.
Evaluate the filtered material for microplastics.

steps.title: Transfer sediment for macroplastic analysis
steps.instruction: Place a 39 L container beneath the K‑grab, open the grab jaws, scoop all sediment into the container with a stainless‑steel scoop, then measure and record the sediment volume.

substeps.instruction: Position a 39 L container under the K‑grab.
Open the grab jaws.
Transfer all sediment into the container using a stainless‑steel scoop.
Measure the sediment volume and record the value.

steps.title: Wash sediment and collect macroplastics
steps.instruction: Move the sediment to a stainless‑steel bucket fitted with a 5 mm mesh, wash it with surface seawater while a mesh filter on the intake hose retains particles larger than 5 mm, then identify, record, and store the recovered macroplastic items.

substeps.instruction: Transfer sediment to a stainless‑steel bucket equipped with a 5 mm mesh.
Wash the sediment with surface seawater.
Attach a mesh filter to the intake hose to capture macroplastics > 5 mm.
Collect the retained macroplastic items.
Identify each macroplastic item.
Record item details (type, size, location).
Store the items appropriately for later analysis.
